description: L2.3 resolution cache change trace. Each family fixes an initial virtual filesystem, a request set, and ordered generations of explicit changes. The native observer replays the same states with the vendored TypeScript 6.0.3 and records fresh results per generation; the Rust contract replays them through the generation cache and compares fresh, reused, and native results.

families.description: The handoff's minimal example: an unresolved relative import is cached as NotFound, an unrelated change reuses it, and creating the missing file recomputes it.
A resolved relative target depends on existence, not content: editing the target reuses, deleting recomputes to NotFound, recreating recomputes to resolved.
Adding a higher-priority extension twin invalidates the probed negative candidates only; a lower-priority twin that was never probed is ignored.

A missing parent directory is a recorded negative dependency: creating the empty directory recomputes (measured over-invalidation), then the file, delete, and recreate transitions each recompute, and an unrelated sibling reuses.
package.json exports edits, manifest deletion, invalid JSON, and a node_modules swap each recompute; an unrelated source edit reuses.
Node10 package `types` field edits and a typesVersions map addition recompute both the package root and a subpath request through the shared package.json content dependency.

Every option in tsc's affectsModuleResolution set is part of the key: paths, moduleSuffixes, customConditions, and moduleResolution changes start fresh keys, while returning to a previous option identity reuses its retained entries.

Review R1: option identity is structural. customConditions ["a,b"] and ["a","b"], reordering, an empty list and an absent option are distinct identities (each starts fresh, never reusing another identity's entry), moduleSuffixes element boundaries likewise, and returning to an earlier identity reuses its retained entries.
Review R1: paths substitutions and patterns keep their element boundaries in the identity: one substitution containing a comma is not two substitutions, and a pattern split is a different map.
The resolution mode is part of the key: import and require conditions produce two entries for one specifier, both depend on the same package.json, and an unrelated file creation reuses both.

Wildcard automatic @types discovery (types: ["*"], the only form 6.0.3 enumerates) depends on the type root directory listing and each candidate package.json; adding, removing, hiding, and null-typings packages change the name set and the per-name resolutions accordingly.

Explicit typeRoots make the primary lookup authoritative for automatic names: adding a package under the custom root recomputes only that name, removing it yields NotFound, and a package appearing under node_modules/@types is never probed and therefore reused.
libReplacement resolution of @typescript/lib-* from the synthetic containing file is a distinct request kind with tsc's isolated Node10 option set; installing and removing the package recompute it.

On a case-insensitive host the containing directory and dependency paths fold to the TypeScript file-name case fold while the specifier spelling stays exact: two containing spellings share one entry, a differently spelled specifier is a separate entry, and an edit under another spelling still invalidates.

A directory symlink into node_modules: retargeting the link recomputes through the realpath alias, preserveSymlinks starts a fresh identity with lexical results, retargeting under preserveSymlinks recomputes through the changed manifest bytes, and removing the link yields NotFound.

Keys are per containing directory: the same specifier from two directories yields two entries, and a change below one directory touches only that entry. Moving the last file out of a directory removes that directory in the host model, so the NotFound row that observed the directory is recomputed without changing (measured over-invalidation).
A reader holding an older generation keeps its values while later generations recompute; releasing the reader drops the retained entries.
Two containing files in one directory (two projects with the same option identity) share one entry; a project with a different identity gets its own.
Cached host-level rows are rebound to each generation's own source membership: adding an import changes program order and ids while the unchanged row is reused.
A host I/O failure aborts the candidate without touching the published view or caching a NotFound; once the host recovers the next generation recomputes from the published state.

Cancellation while building a candidate and cancellation just before publish both leave the published generation intact; the following generation recomputes everything the cancelled candidates had produced.
Retention limits evict least recently used entries at publish; evicted keys are recomputed fresh with identical results while retained keys reuse.

The implied node format of a source depends on its nearest package.json: editing the root manifest's type, adding a nearer manifest, and deleting the root manifest each recompute only the affected files.

A config graph depends on the root text, every extended file (present or absent), the include directory listings, and the node_modules lookup of a package extends; the driver receives typed rebuild requests instead of resolver-level invalidation.

A case-insensitive host still returns option-supplied display paths. Preserve both display and canonical typeRoots/rootDirs identities; returning to the original spellings reuses the corresponding entries.

Containing directory spelling is a result input even when canonical paths coincide. Config-file display spelling also controls implicit type roots. Distinct spellings must match fresh native/Rust results.
